result:
**Rebuttal (Debater A, for c = 1/25)**

B's upper bound is valid but loose. A random cut only shows c ≤ 1/8, and that is not the question. The regularity argument in Step 1 shows the reduced graph R is triangle-free, so the problem reduces to a weighted version of the triangle-free case. For triangle-free graphs, Erdős, Faudree, Pach and Spencer showed that n²/25 deletions always suffice to make the graph bipartite, and the balanced blow-up of C₅ shows this is tight. So c ≤ 1/25 + o(1) follows from the reduction, which is stronger than B's 1/8.

B's objection to the lower bound also fails. The C₅ blow-up is not the T₄(n) example. Its parts have size n/5, but an independent set can use at most two pairwise non-adjacent parts, and the part-internal graphs are sparse and triangle-free with α = O(√(n log n)). So α = o(n). Its clique number is 4, so it is K₅-free. It needs n²/25 deletions, giving c ≥ 1/25.

B also has not offered a triangle-free weighted construction beating C₅. B's stated question, whether the bound is attained, is answered by the C₅ blow-up. B's position therefore reduces to a bound that is weaker than the one the reduction gives.
